rows.annotation: Lipid A phosphoethanolamine transferase EptA catalyzing addition of phosphoethanolamine to lipid A.
rows.evidence: Experimentally characterized EptA homologs from Pseudomonas aeruginosa (46.10% identity) and Pseudomonas syringae (45.10%) add phosphoethanolamine to lipid A. Query phosphoethanolamine-transferase domains and five predicted transmembrane helices support this assignment. Aluminum-sensitive fitness phenotypes provide supporting stress context; weak cofitness correlations do not establish a pathway. Exact lipid A modification position and zinc regulation are not assigned to the query.
rows.reasoning_trace: Tier A is supported by experimentally characterized homologs above 40% identity with explicit lipid A phosphoethanolamine-transfer activity, corroborated by query domain annotations. Available evidence includes homolog summaries, domains, fitness, cofitness, neighborhoods, STRING associations, and query membrane topology. Sulfatase/hydrolase and OpgE glucan-transferase alternatives are less supported: broad domain and orthogroup labels do not outweigh experimentally demonstrated lipid A modification in close homologs.

rows.kblh_paperblast_evidence:
PROTEIN SEQUENCE ORIGINATES FROM BACTERIA: Pseudomonas putida
[[BEGIN SUMMARY]]
%Identity to query protein: 46.30
Homolog originates from: Pseudomonas aeruginosa PAO1
Evidence type: comparative
This gene was analyzed for non-synonymous SNPs across 22 strains relative to PAO1. A total of 49 SNPs were identified across the isolates.
[[END SUMMARY]]
[[BEGIN SUMMARY]]
%Identity to query protein: 46.30
Homolog originates from: Pseudomonas aeruginosa PAO1
Evidence type: experimental
This gene encodes a phosphoethanolamine lipid A transferase. The protein was found to be upregulated by 3O-C12-HSL and showed decreased expression levels when treated with compound C01 compared to 3O-C12-HSL (Table 1, Table 2).
[[END SUMMARY]]
[[BEGIN SUMMARY]]
%Identity to query protein: 46.10
Homolog originates from: Pseudomonas aeruginosa UCBPP-PA14
Evidence type: experimental
Named EptAPa, this gene encodes a functional phosphoethanolamine (pEtN) transferase that strictly modifies the 4' phosphate group of lipid A in both E. coli and P. aeruginosa. Its transcription is induced by extracellular zinc (Zn2+) via the ColRS two-component system. Deletion of the gene abolishes Zn2+-dependent pEtN addition to lipid A, and its overexpression induces the modification regardless of zinc presence.
[[END SUMMARY]]
[[BEGIN SUMMARY]]
%Identity to query protein: 45.10
Homolog originates from: Pseudomonas syringae pv. phaseolicola 1448A
Evidence type: experimental
This gene encodes the phosphoethanolamine transferase EptA in P. syringae pv. phaseolicola 1448A. In a $ΔeptA$ knockout strain, P-EtN-modified lipid A species are absent. The enzyme is responsible for adding P-EtN to the phosphate groups of lipid A, which reduces the overall net negative charge of the molecule.
[[END SUMMARY]]
[[BEGIN SUMMARY]]
%Identity to query protein: 45.10
Homolog originates from: Escherichia coli O127:H6 str. E2348/69
Evidence type: experimental
This gene, encoding the predicted metal dependent hydrolase EptA, was activated by Ler in EPEC strain E2348/69, showing 2-fold activation in mid-log phase and 4-fold activation in late-log phase.
[[END SUMMARY]]
[[BEGIN SUMMARY]]
%Identity to query protein: 44.20
Homolog originates from: Pseudomonas aeruginosa PAO1
Evidence type: experimental
This gene (also identified as PA14_21210) was found to be upregulated in P. aeruginosa in response to bile. The authors utilized a PA3310 (PA14_21210) TnM mutant to demonstrate that the bile-induced increase in polymyxin B tolerance occurs independently of this gene.
[[END SUMMARY]]
[[BEGIN SUMMARY]]
%Identity to query protein: 43.20
Homolog originates from: Salmonella typhimurium (strain LT2 / SGSC1412 / ATCC 700720)
Evidence type: comparative
This gene encodes the phosphoethanolamine transferase EptA (PmrC) and was identified via sequence analysis in K. pneumoniae 16BU137, K. pneumoniae 19PDR22, and K. pneumoniae KP20191015.
[[END SUMMARY]]
[[BEGIN SUMMARY]]
%Identity to query protein: 43.00
Homolog originates from: Kosakonia pseudosacchari
Evidence type: computational
The gene encodes the non-mobile colistin resistance enzyme NMCR-2.
[[END SUMMARY]]

rows.conservation_breadth:
[[BEGIN CONSERVATION BREADTH]]
Counted over EVERY homolog found for this query, before the per-source display caps that apply to the other evidence blocks.
Distinct organisms with a homolog: 42 (in 19 genera)
Query organism: Pseudomonas putida
Organisms OTHER than the query's own with a homolog: 41 (18 genera other than Pseudomonas)
%Identity to query across these homologs: 38.4-100.0
Meaning: breadth of conservation, not function. A homolog in an organism other than the query's own is evidence the protein is real and under selection even when no function can be named, and supports calling it a CONSERVED hypothetical protein; homologs confined to the query's own organism do not. More organisms and more genera mean broader conservation. This NEVER constrains the specific function.
[[END CONSERVATION BREADTH]]
